conviction_note: The only thing in this capture that is not June-quarter wire copy is a filing-verified pattern of a 10% holder buying ~$24m of stock in the open market above the current price while the company itself made an unusual intraquarter 8-K disclosure the same evening; that is a mild upside asymmetry, so I take about a sixth of the 7.5% median reaction.

findings.finding: 10% owner Globalharvest bought roughly 1.77m shares for ~$23.7m in the open market on 7/7-7/9 at $13.00-$13.50 (Form 4s of 07/08, 07/09, 07/10 plus a 13D/A accepted 2026-07-09T20:15:20Z), entirely above the pre-print close of $12.87, taking affiliate-held stock to roughly 42-45% of the shares out; and the company filed a voluntary item-8.01 8-K 90 minutes after that 13D/A (accepted 2026-07-09T21:54:02Z) reporting buyback progress only one month into a $100m authorisation.

findings.why_not_priced: The 8-K and 13D/A bodies are not in the capture and the news channel returned zero items for AVO across all eleven sweeps, so this reached the tape only through insider-trade aggregators and one StockTwits thread. If it were priced, AVO would not be trading $0.15-$0.75 below the entire range at which the largest informed buyer took ~$24m of stock six weeks earlier, and the 20d run-in would not be -2.1% on unremarkable volume (400-700k against a 518k average).
findings.independence: The company's own $100m authorisation (announced 2026-06-03, referenced in the same StockTwits digest at 2026-06-09T14:51:07Z) and the January rights plan (8-K items 1.01/3.03/5.03 plus 8-A12B accepted 2026-01-22T21:05:55Z, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1802974/000110465926097078/xslSCHEDULE_13G_X02/primary_doc.xml is the 13G, the 8-K is accession-indexed in filings.json) point the same way: the board is treating the stock as cheap and the float as contested. Note this finding and that corroboration share the StockTwits digest as the source of the dollar amounts, so they are one source cluster on magnitude and two on the underlying filings.

baseline_tension: It cuts mildly against the tape - the run-in is -2.1% over 20 days and the stock is 16% off its 52-week high - while the filings say the best-informed buyer was paying more than spot; the reaction history (5 of 7 up, 7.5% median) is not informative on direction.
